title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 19 — RUNNER's connector entry names the own-port boot by what it is, and the packaged-automation board's inventory clause judges the switch
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 19 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor (claim `6305778491`, PM loop round 34). It applies round 18's two carried checklist-text findings, PR #25018's out-of-scope findings as its ACCEPT `6305381435` and landing record `6305762608` carry them.

Only checklist text changes, in two files: `RUNNER.md` (two spellings) and `areas/automation.json` (`automation.setup-packaged-automation-board` `acceptance[1]`, one `revision` bump and one `history` row naming PR #25018). There is no product code, test, pin or changeset text, no new item, and every item id is kept.

- Base `73432299c0` (`origin/main` when the branch was cut, and still `origin/main` when this body was written).
- objectui sources were read at the console pin `cf153eb2e535` (`.objectui-sha` on `main`) with `git show`: `packagedFlows.ts` blob `a85c96d28e5a` and `PackagedAutomationPage.tsx` blob `f4aa90e11d32`, the same blobs round 18 cited. The server side was read at the base.
- The live reading at the pin is NOT MEASURED. The sources were read, not run.

## 1. `RUNNER.md`: the connector environment-facts entry

The entry named the dogfood §0 own-port boot "isolated" twice, the phrasing a runner reads as the `isolated` tenancy posture. Both are respelled in the voice rounds 17 and 18 used in the area files (round 18: "a dogfood-§0 isolated boot on a non-3000 port" → "a dogfood-§0 boot on its own non-3000 port", and "an isolated boot without it dials 3000" → "a boot on its own port without it dials 3000"). This is a plain textual edit, two lines, and no line is re-wrapped. In the quotes below, `PORT` stands for the angle-bracket port placeholder the file spells.

| line | old | new |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `:260` | `- **An isolated boot on a non-3000 port breaks the showcase's self-pinging connectors` | `- **A boot on its own non-3000 port breaks the showcase's self-pinging connectors` |
| `:269` | `` back, so the dogfood §0 isolated boot — `objectstack dev … -p PORT` with the env `` | `` back, so the dogfood §0 boot on its own port — `objectstack dev … -p PORT` with the env `` |

`git diff --stat`: `RUNNER.md | 4 ++--`.

Every `isolated` in `RUNNER.md` at the base, each read in its context:

| line | text | sense | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `:141` | rule 8's probe list: "`group` beside `isolated`" | posture (the opposite posture a probe tries) | kept |
| `:260` | "An isolated boot on a non-3000 port breaks the showcase's self-pinging connectors" | the own-port boot | respelled |
| `:269` | "the dogfood §0 isolated boot — `objectstack dev … -p PORT` with the env untouched" | the own-port boot | respelled |
| `:519` | the walled-boot entry: "`os serve` boots `group` and `isolated`" | posture (walled mode) | kept |
| `:527` | "`OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=group` or `isolated`" | posture | kept |
| `:528` | "`resolveTenancyPosture()` … reads as `isolated`" | posture | kept |
| `:591` | the walled-boot measurement: "under `isolated` with the other two set" | posture (walled mode) | kept |

That is 7 at the base and 5 at the head, all 5 posture texts. Two other forms of the word are not the boot's name and are left: `:9`, "environment isolation (§0)", names the dogfood skill's section, and `:319`, "do NOT isolate a package install", is a verb.

## 2. `automation.setup-packaged-automation-board` `acceptance[1]` (revision 7 → 8)

The clause said "default all On, an obsolete-status flow excepted". That holds for the row's switch, the activation flag. It does not hold for the Activation badge beside the switch, which `steps[3]` (revision 7) reads as "Not running here", switch still checked, for the two policy-unbound schedule flows on a default boot.

**clause, old:**

> inventory: the flows table lists exactly the packaged flows (default all On, an obsolete-status flow excepted: the engine holds it disabled, so its switch reads Off) and the packaged-actions section renders beside it; tenant/org-authored flows are ABSENT

**clause, new:**

> inventory: the flows table lists exactly the packaged flows (each row's switch, the activation flag, is checked by default, an obsolete-status flow excepted: the engine holds it disabled, so its switch is unchecked) and the packaged-actions section renders beside it; tenant/org-authored flows are ABSENT. This clause judges the switch, not the badge beside it: on a default boot the two policy-unbound schedule flows keep a checked switch while their badge reads 'Not running here' (steps[3]), and that reading does not fail this clause

**verify:** the old text is kept whole, and this is appended:

> Score each row's switch against the enabled field of its row in the same GET /api/v1/automation/_status read steps[3] takes: the page checks the switch exactly where that field is not false (joinPackagedFlows in packagedFlows.ts; the Switch's checked prop in PackagedAutomationPage.tsx), and the engine sets it false only for an obsolete or invalid status or a ledger toggle (isFlowEnabled, service-automation engine.ts). OS_AUTOMATION_SCHEDULED_WORK_ENABLED moves the badge, never the flag: on a fresh boot the only unchecked switch is the obsolete-status flow's (showcase_approver_bindings), whether that variable is exported or not. The badge (data-testid packaged-flow-activation) is steps[3]'s reading, reconciled there against the row's unboundCause: ⛔ do not score a 'Not running here' badge as a switch reading Off, nor read a checked switch as a flow that runs

**oracle** (`dom`) and **evidence** ("row list vs the two API reads, side by side") are unchanged. They match `steps[3]`, which compares the rendered rows against `GET /api/v1/meta/flow` and `GET /api/v1/automation/_status`. The clause still judges what the page renders, against those two reads.

Why the new text holds:

- At the pin, `joinPackagedFlows` sets `enabled: state.enabled !== false`, and the row's `Switch` renders `checked={row.enabled}`. The badge is a separate element (`data-testid="packaged-flow-activation"`, `data-reading` from `activationReading`), which reads `off` when the flag is off, `not-running` when the flag is on and the row carries an `unboundCause`, and `on` otherwise.
- At the base, `getFlowRuntimeStates()` takes `enabled` from `isFlowEnabled(name)`, which is false only for `flowStatusDisabled` (status `obsolete` or `invalid`) or `flowLedgerDisabled` (the activation ledger). `describeUnboundReason` returns its `deployment_policy` cause only for an enabled flow, so the scheduled-work switch moves the badge and never the flag.
- At the base, `allFlows` still declares 32 flows: one obsolete (`showcase_approver_bindings`) and two `type: 'schedule'` (`showcase_scheduled_digest`, `showcase_task_due_reminder`), as round 18 derived at `93e6c1a5f8`. `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/` has no change between the two commits.

## How the edits were made and checked

- `RUNNER.md`: a plain textual edit of the two lines, shown above.
- `automation.json`: the scripted span editor of rounds 17 and 18, unchanged (sha256 `b0fa4606c135…`, identical). It never re-serialises the file. Dry run, then `--write`, both printing: `OK … A1 doc == old + declared ops; A2 21 unedited items + 5 top-level keys value-equal; A3 per item below; A4 text outside the 1 edited item spans byte-identical`, with `automation.setup-packaged-automation-board: revision 7 -> 8; 7 leaf paths changed, all within [acceptance.1.clause, acceptance.1.verify, revision, history.7]`.
- A separate whole-branch check against the base agrees. Exactly the two files changed. One item changed, with revision +1 and exactly one appended row (`revision`, `date`, `change`, `ref`). Nothing changed outside `acceptance[1].clause` and `acceptance[1].verify`, and that clause's `oracle` and `evidence` are unchanged.
- The new history row carries the placeholder ref `#PENDING-24579R19`, because a row's `ref` names this PR and the PR had no number yet (the rounds 6–18 precedent). The next commit on this branch swaps in this PR's number and changes nothing else. The gates are re-run on that head, and the report comment on #24579 records them.
- A control-byte scan of both files finds none.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 13 commands on the 2 paths, against merge base `73432299c` of `origin/main`. At head `a6a963a5f9` each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe, and each exited 0:

`node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --self-test` · `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` · `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `pnpm check:doc-authoring` · `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` · `pnpm check:gitlink-declared` · `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `pnpm check:platform-checklist` · `pnpm check:refd-timer-probe` · `pnpm check:watch-hint-literal`

The first run of `check:doc-formula-expressions` refused with exit 3, a prerequisite: `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` were not built in this worktree. Both were built under the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, held 2 s, waited 0 s), and the rerun exited 0. `--ran`, with an exit code on every line, reads "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", a derived zero.

No per-PR CI job runs `pnpm check:platform-checklist`, so this local reading is its evidence. The base column was taken in this worktree with both files restored to the base's blobs, then restored to `HEAD` and proven equal by blob hash, with `git diff HEAD` empty:

| reading | base `73432299c0` | head `a6a963a5f9` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| exit | 0 | 0 |
| items | 16 areas, 328 items (323 active, 1 planned) | 16 areas, 328 items (323 active, 1 planned) |
| line citations | 0 survive across 21 swept documents | 0 survive across 21 swept documents |
| symbol anchors | 979/989 against 434 cited sources, 10 on the named residual (#16898), 18 file floors held | 979/989 against 434 cited sources, 10 on the named residual (#16898), 18 file floors held |

No anchor and no line citation is added. The new verify text names `joinPackagedFlows`, `isFlowEnabled` and the two files in prose, as the item already cites objectui.

`git merge-tree --write-tree` exited 0 against each of:

- `origin/main` `73432299c0`;
- PR #25021's head `2e76ecfc31` (it changes `areas/records-forms.json`);
- PR #25024's head `356172a1f9` (it changes `FOLLOW-UPS.md`).

Neither of those PRs touches `RUNNER.md` or `areas/automation.json`. Their file lists were read over REST, 7 and 41 files.

There is no ablation, because no tested behaviour changed. `skip-changeset` was re-measured: no `files[]` entry of the 73 non-private manifests (86 tracked `package.json` files) reaches outside its own package or names `docs/qa`, and the repo root is private.

## Acceptance notes

- **The same respelling is still owed in the area-level fixture recipes, outside every item.** Rounds 17 and 18 respelled item texts, and this round's surface is `RUNNER.md` and one clause. At the base, 11 strings in the area-level `fixtures` recipes of four area files still name the own-port boot or its DB "isolated", with no posture word beside them:
  - `attachments-storage.json`: `qa-scratch-authz` (`requires[2]`, `teardown`) and `qa-media-constraints` (`requires[1]`, `teardown`);
  - `automation.json`: `qa-flow-status-doors` (`requires[1]`, `requires[2]`, `teardown`);
  - `records-forms.json`: `qa-feeds-disabled` (`requires[1]`, `teardown`);
  - `search.json`: `qa-contributor-bound-member` (`requires[2]`, `teardown`).

  One of them, `qa-flow-status-doors.requires[2]`, points at this entry as "RUNNER.md, the isolated-boot/OS_PORT standing fact". After this PR the entry's title no longer says "isolated", so that pointer names it by words it no longer carries. `records-forms.json` is in open PR #25021. This is noted for the wave anchor, and not filed.
